notes:
Account: Ember IDE Systems - building an IDE copilot plugin (VSCode + JetBrains). Focus: super-low TTFT for streaming completions and deterministic token budgets for UX predictability.

Recent timeline - quick bullets:
- 2025-11-10 discovery call (AE: Sofia) - fast intro; they stressed 'must feel instant in-editor' and not block typing.
- 2026-01-28 product demo (SE: Arjun) - showed streaming + function-calling, customer asked about backpressure handling in VSCode extension. Fireflies id ff-2026-02-12-ember-demo.
- 2026-02-20 security questionnaire returned (SOC2 + SSO required). Mentioned KMS + 13mo retention as preferred.
- 2026-03-01 POC kickoff (internal): spinning up dedicated pool for low-latency path; defining TTFT targets and token budget policies.
- 2026-03-09 perf sync: agreed initial SLAs: TTFT cold <= 120ms, warm <= 40ms, 95th pct token latency jitter < 20ms. Throughput target: 250 concurrent editor streams across 5 regions.
- 2026-03-10 SE notes: need to test backpressure scenario when user types faster than streaming can deliver; strategy: client-side buffering + server push + early-stop heuristics.
- Current POC: 2-week perf run on Dedicated GPUs, measuring cold-start distribution, KV-cache warmup, and quantized model fallback quality hit.

Use-case / requirements (short):
- Primary: in-editor code completion and multi-line suggestions (streaming).
- TTFT is priority metric for UX; token budget tuning required to avoid runaway completions and to enforce predictable latency.
- Client must support graceful backpressure; extension cannot freeze the editor.
- Model pinning: want ability to pin stable minor model revisions (e.g., ember-compat-2.7q) and auto-fallback to quantized versions under load.
- Cost sensitivity moderate: prefer Dedicated for predictable perf but will evaluate Hosted if cost/latency tradeoffs favorable.

Security & compliance:
- Must support SSO/SAML and enterprise audit logs. KMS integration required for keys. Data residency: US/EU options requested.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- TTFT targets met 90%+ for warm requests.
- Jitter under threshold (95th pct < 20ms).
- No editor freeze during simulated high input rate (backpressure test).
- Token budget enforcement prevents >2x expected token burn per session.

Quotes from customer:
- 'If the suggestion feels laggy, devs will turn it off' (lead eng).
- 'We need predictable token costs more than raw max quality' (product lead).

Next steps / Action items:
- Redwood: provision dedicated pool and baseline perf harness (Arjun) - due 2026-03-15.
- Ember: provide representative extension telemetry and typical session traces - due 2026-03-12.
- Security: exchange KMS integration doc and retention policy (drive:/deals/ember/security-faq.md).
- AE: prepare pricing scenarios for Dedicated vs Hosted with model-quantization tiers.
